content.text: This is a P1 bug where hazard classes with a division (e.g. "5.1", "2.1") never match the segregation table. Let me look at the source file.

Found the bug: `mustSegregate` calls `primaryClass()` which strips divisions (e.g. `"5.1"` → `"5"`), but the `SEGREGATION` table is keyed by the full division label (`"5.1"`, `"2.1"`, etc.) for classes that have divisions. So any hazard class with a division never resolves to a table entry. The fix is to look up by the trimmed class string as-is, not the primary-class-only reduction.

content.text:
All tests pass, full suite is green.

Fixed INC-86 in `src/cargo/hazmat.ts:17-22`: `mustSegregate` was reducing class labels to their primary number via `primaryClass()` before looking them up in `SEGREGATION`, but that table keys divisional classes (`"2.1"`, `"4.1"`, `"5.1"`, `"5.2"`) by their full label — so `primaryClass("5.1")` produced `"5"`, which never matched anything. Now it looks up the trimmed class string directly. Added a regression test in `test/hazmat.test.ts` covering the incident's acceptance cases.
